title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
Given two sorted integer arrays `arr1` and `arr2`, merge them into a single sorted array and return it.

The resulting array should contain all elements from both arrays in non-decreasing order.

editorial.approach: Maintain two pointers, `i = 0` for `arr1` and `j = 0` for `arr2`. Compare arr1[i] and arr2[j], push the smaller one into a result array, and increment its pointer. Append remaining elements after one array is exhausted.
editorial.complexity: O(n + m) time / O(n + m) space

hints: You can combine the arrays first and then sort them, but that is not optimal.
Use two pointers, `i` starting at 0 for `arr1` and `j` starting at 0 for `arr2`.
Compare `arr1[i]` and `arr2[j]`. Push the smaller value to the result array and increment that pointer. Repeat until one array is finished, then push the remaining elements of the other array.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Concatenate both arrays using `.concat()` or spread syntax, then sort the merged array in non-decreasing order.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use two pointers to merge the elements in linear O(n + m) time by comparing values at each step.

interviewExplanation: A brute-force sort takes O((n+m) log(n+m)) time. Since both inputs are already sorted, we can merge them in O(n + m) time by comparing front elements with two pointers and appending sequentially.
